decisions.mark: names MBEDTLS_THREADING_C and MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD as the gating macros
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "Even then, the index shows only the listed globals and the heap mutex... or build with `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` and `MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD`." | WHY: The answer names both MBEDTLS_THREADING_C and MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD as the gating macros, saying the mutex code sits behind THREADING_C and that PTHREAD is also off by default.

decisions.mark: states that the shipped mbedtls_config.h leaves BOTH threading macros undefined, so a default build defines neither
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "`MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` has default state `off`, declared at `include/mbedtls/mbedtls_config.h:3787`." and "`MBEDTLS_THREADING_PTHREAD` is also `off` by default (`mbedtls_config.h:2196`)." | WHY: The answer states both threading macros are off by default in the shipped mbedtls_config.h, so a default build defines neither.

decisions.mark: concludes that a default build of mbedtls creates no threads at all, and that the pthread example compiles to a stub main under that condition
decisions.detail: QUOTE: NONE | WHY: The answer says the library spawns no threads and `threading.c` compiles to nothing by default. It never says the pthread example compiles to a stub main. It says the sample programs are "not built by default", which is not the stub-main fact.

decisions.mark: states BOTH halves of the contrast: that nothing in library/ creates a thread, AND that library/ nonetheless supplies the mutex abstraction used by threaded callers
decisions.detail: QUOTE: NONE | WHY: The answer says the library spawns no threads and describes mutexes behind MBEDTLS_THREADING_C. It never says library/ supplies the mutex abstraction for threaded callers. It says the library is not thread-safe and has no locks by default, and the thread spawns it lists are in programs/.
